task\\u0027s pull request was carried by 2 runs. Each one\\u0027s handoff follows, in\\r\\ndispatch order \\u2014 the run that opened the work first, its follow-ups after it.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Run 1 of 2 \\u00B7 d60add1e]\\r\\n\\r\\n- **What now exists.** Closeout classifies and records advisory human threads (\\u0060AdvisoryReviewThreads\\u0060, \\u0060AdvisoryReviewThreadsObserved\\u0060) and excludes them from dispatch; \\u0060HumanThreadReplyParked\\u0060 parks a drafted reply for a person\\u0027s declined or routed thread, answered by \\u0060h9k review resolve\\u0060\\u0027s existing three choices; \\u0060h9k pr reply\\u0060 is the platform\\u0027s guarded posting path with \\u0060h9k pr reply-guard\\u0060 as the \\u0060PreToolUse\\u0060 hook behind it; \\u0060TaskReopened.HumanReviewThreads\\u0060 carries each observed thread\\u0027s author and link onto the task. The Decisions Log entry sits at the tail under \\u0060PLACEHOLDER-7d8d1fec\\u0060.\\n- **The non-obvious shape.** The park\\u0027s trustworthy half is *whose thread it is*, read off the provider at dispatch and carried on the task; the disposition is the session\\u0027s own claim, and every design decision here keeps those two straight. If you extend this, do not start trusting a session\\u0027s \\u0060kind=\\u0060 tag: \\u0060ReviewThreadOutcome.IsHuman\\u0060\\u0027s doc says why it is a record and not a gate. Two mechanical traps: \\u0060Apply(TaskReopened)\\u0060 must copy before clearing, because a caller may pass the aggregate\\u0027s own list back; and \\u0060AgentSpawnRequest.GuardsReviewThreadReplies\\u0060 has to be set at *every* spawn site that puts a session into a follow-up run\\u0027s worktree, not just the launcher, which now means the review loop\\u0027s and the gates\\u0027 sessions too.\\n- **What I left undone, deliberately.** \\u0060gh pr comment\\u0060 is not refused, so a top-level reply to a person is still reachable; refusing it would break the review-body instruction from Decisions Log #62, which this task was told not to touch. Bot thread handling and the merge bar are unchanged. The hook was exercised by running \\u0060h9k pr reply-guard\\u0060 against real payloads, not against a live Claude Code session, which nothing in this repository can do from a test; if it ever needs verifying end to end, that is an operator running one follow-up and reading the run\\u0027s stderr.\\n- **One suspicion I could not pin down.** \\u0060h9k pr reply\\u0060 resolves its run as \\u0060task.CurrentRunId\\u0060, so a stale session whose run was superseded mid-lap would have its reply recorded against the live run instead. I could not construct a case where that matters (the platform supersedes such a run anyway, and the raw \\u0060gh\\u0060 route it replaces recorded nothing at all), so I left it rather than adding a generation fence on an informational append.\\r\\n\\r\\n[Run 2 of 2 \\u00B7 0eaac473]\\r\\n\\r\\n- Four Copilot findings on PR #397 are fixed and folded into the commits that own them (no review-feedback commits): the reply guard now refuses every mutating method in every spelling plus the number-free \\u0060pulls/comments/\\u003Cid\\u003E\\u0060 edit/delete route; \\u0060h9k pr reply\\u0060 fences its run stream for existence; \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060 says what the owner did with each drafted reply instead of always calling it unsent; and an unreadable thread opener is carried as \\u0060null\\u0060 so it can never classify as advisory.\\n- The gotcha for anyone working this branch: **\\u0060h9k pr reply\\u0060 is unusable from a session on it.** The installed CLI predates the command and the worktree build refuses against the live schema. Do not run \\u0060h9k doctor --yes\\u0060 to get around that; it would migrate the database out from under the running 0.9.1 daemon. Use the \\u0060gh\\u0060 reply route for bot threads and log the interaction. Second gotcha: autosquash onto \\u0060origin/main\\u0060 silently rebases onto a moved main and invalidates your test run; use \\u0060git merge-base origin/main HEAD\\u0060 as the base and check tree identity against the tip you actually tested, not the pre-fixup tip.\\n- Deliberately left undone: the versioned append Copilot asked for on \\u0060h9k pr reply\\u0060 (declined with the codebase\\u0027s own fenced-vs-unfenced rule; it would lose the record of an already-public reply), and the three body-level findings, which are filed as ideas \\u0060f9df6908\\u0060, \\u0060a69f1595\\u0060, \\u00605998b58a\\u0060 rather than grown\\n\\n[Truncated at 4000 characters.
